reply:
Good. That's a real decision, not a hopeful one — you've looked at your own failure mode and planned around it instead of pretending you'd handle it better in the moment.

Two things, and then I'll get out of your way.

"Out" is worth picturing concretely. Do you get out of the car, or does he? If you're the one driving, the exit is different than if he is. Knowing the physical move — door, keys, walk — means the closing line has somewhere to go instead of hanging in the air while you both sit there.

And the thing you said — "I only get the one shot" — isn't quite true, and it's worth loosening. You get one shot at *this* telling, in this car, tonight. But tomorrow morning is a different conversation, and you're allowed to have it or not have it. If he goes quiet and weird, that's not the verdict on the whole thing. It's one man's first thirty seconds with information he's never had. He might come back to it a day later, badly, and that still counts.

The point of the sentence isn't his response. It's that you said it and didn't take it back. That part is entirely yours, and he can't get it wrong.
